title: How college football teams handled grounded flights, from tarmac walkthroughs to bus rides
author: Matt Baker
content:
Colorado State did a team walkthrough on the tarmac. Utah held meetings. Tennessee catered Texas Roadhouse.

As administrators and staffers worked through the complicated logistics stemming from Friday’s nationwide air traffic shutdown, players and coaches were left with hours to fill. Programs attacked the issue differently before planes were cleared to take off Friday evening after four-plus hours.

The Rams got some work in at the Northern Colorado Regional Airport during their delay before flying to Washington State. Colorado State planned to do a walkthrough later in the day once it arrived at its hotel in Pullman, so the work wasn’t unscheduled, exactly. It just had a photogenic background.

The Rams had a team meal brought to the airport, flew uneventfully to Pullman and hit their initially planned lights-out time at the hotel (9:30 p.m. PT).

The Volunteers returned to campus, where staffers scrambled to get a dinner catered by the steakhouse chain. Staffers unloaded the plane, then had to reload it a few hours later. When they got to College Station, Texas, late Friday night, the Hilton College Station staff was prepared to welcome them as if nothing happened.

Undefeated Utah’s delay before flying to Arizona was relatively uneventful — some meetings and sitting around. Kansas State waited for about an hour and a half on its plane before heading back to the facility for meetings. The Wildcats finalized their Saturday morning flight to TCU around midnight. Kansas State lost 20-10 Saturday afternoon, falling to 4-6 this season.

Utah State got creative, asking fans on social media for movie or music recommendations to pass the time. Among the suggestions: the 1987 John Candy/Steve Martin comedy “Planes, Trains and Automobiles” and the Aggies’ 2019 game against this week’s opponent, San Diego State, that featured a 293-yard day from former Utah State star and current Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love.

Most of the athletes played games, scrolled social media or watched movies before they, too, deboarded to wait for more information. The Aggies eventually touched down in San Diego, accompanied by Sage, the university police department’s Labrador retriever.

More than a dozen programs had their travel plans altered by the Federal Aviation Administration’s shutdown.

Like Kansas State, Baylor, Minnesota and Arizona State flew out early Saturday for games at BYU, Penn State and UCF, respectively. The Sun Devils landed in Orlando in the early afternoon (Eastern time) for a 5:30 p.m. kickoff. It’s unusual for major football programs to fly on game day, especially for cross-country travel (like Arizona State-UCF).

Several other programs, including Purdue (to Iowa), North Texas (to UTSA) and Auburn (to Mississippi State), opted for bus trips instead of rescheduled flights.

Only one game — No. 19 Ole Miss at Oklahoma — was postponed by a day to Sunday.

This story will be updated.
